specific_objectives: 20.4.2.1 Trainee will be able to explain principles of Aero engine control systems.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of PPT diagrams; Instructor supervision required for diagram interpretation.
intro_questions: What is the primary function of an aero engine control system?
Name two types of engine control systems used in aviation.
Why is the classical control system still relevant in modern training?

development.content:
Definition of Classical Control System
Throttle Lever Operation Principles
Governor Mechanism Functionality
Fuel Flow Regulation Basics
Hydraulic Actuation Systems

RPM Control via Governor
Load Sensing and Response
Mechanical Linkage Geometry
Safety Valves and Limits
Idle and Takeoff Settings

Comparison with Fly-by-Wire
Advantages of Mechanical Systems
Limitations of Classical Design
Maintenance Requirements
Transition to Electronic Control

summary_questions: Explain how the governor maintains constant RPM during load changes.
Describe the role of the mechanical linkage in throttle control.
List three advantages of classical control systems over fly-by-wire.
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note comparing the mechanical feedback loop of the classical system with the electronic feedback loop of the Fly-by-Wire system to be discussed in LP 13.

pft_rows.syllabus: Explanation of Fly by wire control systems using Fly by Wire demonstrator at Control Lab.
